correctness.summary: The reversibility and Floquet obstruction check directly. For S(x,y,z)=(x,-y,-z), the vector field obeys F(Su)=-DS F(u), while div F=-a cos(y) sin(z) is S-odd. A periodic orbit invariant as a set under S can be time-shifted so S gamma(t)=gamma(-t); hence its divergence integral over a period is zero. Liouville's formula then gives product of the two transverse multipliers equal to one, excluding an asymptotically attracting or repelling symmetric periodic orbit and leaving a hyperbolic symmetric orbit necessarily of saddle type. The explicit vertical family has speeds -b for even s and 3b for odd s, giving the stated torus periods. At a=0, the normal equation is X''+(-1)^(k+s)X=0, reproducing the elliptic/hyperbolic parity split. For the central orbit, direct linearization gives X''+a sin(z0-bt)X'+X=0; the stated gauge removes the first derivative and produces u''+[1+(ab/2)cos z-(a^2/4)sin^2 z]u=0. Its monodromy has determinant one, so the discriminant trichotomy is correct. The reverser also conjugates nonsymmetric partner monodromies to inverse spectra.

limitations: The no-attractor statement applies to periodic orbits invariant under the stated reverser, not to all periodic or chaotic invariant sets.
The general reversible-Floquet principle is classical; novelty is confined to this system's explicit consequences.
The Hill reduction does not give a closed-form discriminant for arbitrary a and b.
The source preprint is very recent, so parallel source-specific observations may not yet be indexed.

originality.summary: Reciprocal Floquet spectra and the impossibility of asymptotically stable symmetric periodic orbits are classical consequences of reversible dynamics; those principles are not new. The September 2026 Szumiński-Llibre paper introduces and numerically/analytically studies this trigonometric Nosé-Hoover system but its public abstract emphasizes integrability, averaging and differential-Galois results rather than the present exact symmetric-orbit Floquet audit. Searches did not locate this complete source-specific classification, explicit vertical-family parity formula, or the central Hill reduction elsewhere. Originality is accepted only for that application/synthesis.

scientific_value.summary: The result gives an exact symmetry obstruction against interpreting reversible periodic orbits as attractors and reduces their transverse stability to low-dimensional exact criteria. In a paper whose numerics include dissipative attracting sets, this cleanly separates symmetric periodic geometry from genuinely attracting nonsymmetric dynamics.
